div.div:
opprō^bro (obp- ), no
I.perf., ātum, 1, v. a. ob-probrum, to reproach, taunt, upbraid (ante- and post-class.; “syn.: vitupero, objurgo, reprehendo): opprobrare, probrum obicere,” Fest. p. 187 Müll.: “egone id exprobrem, qui mihimet cupio id opprobrarier?” Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 143 : “rus alicui,” id. Truc. 2, 2, 25 : “adversariis,” Gell. 17, 1, 11 : “mollities cuidam opprobrata acerbe,” id. 3, 5
in lemm.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
